question: For the specialist consultant RFPs from DCRB (real assets), Hawaii ERS (2022 private equity and real assets), INPRS (23-09 alternatives), Missouri LAGERS (private markets), TRS Illinois (FY25 private equity), Arizona PSPRS (non-discretionary), Baltimore BCERS (alternatives), SBCERS (2020 private equity) and Illinois FPIF (2023 private markets), what initial contract terms and renewal or extension options are stated?
gold_answer: DCRB real assets: three-year original agreement. Hawaii ERS 2022 real assets: about three years ending June 30, 2026, with optional three-year extension through June 30, 2029. Hawaii ERS 2022 private equity: three years plus optional two-year extension. INPRS 23-09 alternatives: initial five years, optional renewals under the same terms up to another five years, total at most ten. Missouri LAGERS: initial one year, then the right but not obligation to enter an additional two-year agreement with services and fees agreed by both parties. TRS Illinois FY25 PE: execution to December 31, 2029, at most five years, no extension. Arizona PSPRS: initial three years with two possible one-year extensions. Baltimore BCERS: five-year contract and asks agreement/fee quotes for two two-year options. SBCERS 2020 PE and Illinois FPIF 2023 private markets: no fixed engagement term or renewal option found in these RFPs.
acceptance: Accept concise initial-plus-extension terms per named specialist RFP. Baltimore five years plus two possible two-year options is essential; do not accept 'no term'. Missouri one plus an additional two years is explicitly supported by p7. Hawaii search-completion extensions and INPRS temporary month-to-month continuation are supplementary, not mandatory. Naming the exact RFP set avoids treating every general-consultant RFP as required.
candidate_answer:
The terms below are **proposed RFP terms**, not confirmation of the contracts ultimately signed.

| RFP | Initial term | Renewal or extension stated |
|---|---|---|
| DCRB — real assets | Three years. | No renewal or extension option stated. [RFP, p. 7](DC_Retirement_Board__dcrb-rfp-real-assets-investment-consulting-services.pdf#page=7) |
| Hawaii ERS — 2022 private equity | Three years, beginning around April 1, 2023. | ERS may extend for two years, to 2028. It may also extend at no additional cost solely to finish manager or custodian searches already in progress. [RFP, p. 20](Hawaii_ERS__Private-Equity-RFP-8.25.2022-final.pdf#page=20) |
| Hawaii ERS — 2022 real assets | Approximately three years, from around July 1, 2023, through June 30, 2026. | ERS may extend for three years, through June 30, 2029. A no-additional-cost extension may also be used solely to finish manager searches already underway. [RFP, p. 20](Hawaii_ERS__ERS-REAL-ASSETS-INVESTMENT-CONSULTANT-RFP-2022-06.pdf#page=20) |
| INPRS — RFP 23-09 alternatives | Five years from final contract execution. | One or more renewals on the same terms at INPRS’s option, totaling no more than five additional years; the stated maximum is ten years. The *sample agreement* also provides for a month-to-month holdover of up to six months after expiration unless the parties take written action. [RFP, p. 20](INPRS__RFP-23-09-Alternative-Investment-Consulting-Services-FINAL-10-23-23.pdf#page=20) · [Sample agreement, p. 26](INPRS__RFP-23-09-Alternative-Investment-Consulting-Services-FINAL-10-23-23.pdf#page=26) |
| Missouri LAGERS — private markets | One year, contemplated to begin around September 1, 2024. | LAGERS has the right, but not the obligation, to continue for an additional two years. Expanded services and fees require mutual agreement, satisfactory negotiation, and Board concurrence. [RFP, pp. 7, 19](Missouri_LAGERS__LAGERS-Private-Consultant-RFP-Final.pdf#page=7) |
| TRS Illinois — FY25 private equity | From execution through December 31, 2029, **not to exceed five years**, under the sample agreement. | The sample agreement expressly says the term **may not be extended**. [Sample agreement, pp. 25–26](TRS_Illinois__FY25-RFP-Private-Equity-Investment-Consultant.pdf#page=25) |
| Arizona PSPRS — non-discretionary | Anticipated three years. | Two possible one-year extensions before rebidding. [RFP, p. 8](Arizona_PSPRS__PSPRS_Investment_Consultant_RFP.pdf#page=8) |
| Baltimore BCERS — alternatives | Five years. | The RFP asks bidders whether they will accept **two successive two-year options** and to price all four option years. [RFP, p. 24](Baltimore_BCERS__RFP-Alternatives-Consultant-rev.pdf#page=24) · [Fee schedule, p. 27](Baltimore_BCERS__RFP-Alternatives-Consultant-rev.pdf#page=27) |
| SBCERS — 2020 private equity | **No consultant-contract term specified** in the RFP. | No renewal option specified. It asks firms whether they will refrain from proposing fee increases for five years; the fee form’s assumed 15-year *fund* term is not a consultant-contract term. [RFP, pp. 26–27](SBCERS__2020-Private-Equity-RFP.pdf#page=26) |
| Illinois FPIF — 2023 private markets | **No initial contract term specified** in the RFP. | No renewal or extension option specified. The required 360-day validity of a proposal is an **offer-validity period**, not a contract term. [RFP, p. 6](Illinois_FPIF__Private-Markets-RFP-2023.02.13.pdf#page=6) |
